summaries.demographer: Jailyn Claybon is a 21-year-old Black/African American woman born and living in Jacksonville, Florida, in ZIP code 32246 (Q85-Q89). She has never been married, has no children, and lives with one roommate in a rented two-bedroom apartment while sharing household expenses (Q51-Q55, Q84). She has a high school diploma, some college, CNA certification, CPR/BLS credentials, and is enrolled part time in community college prerequisites toward an ADN (Q90-Q92). Her household and life-course position are typical of an early adult balancing work, school, rent, and family support obligations (Q15-Q18, Q56-Q64).
summaries.behavioral_economist: Jailyn shows strong future orientation around nursing credentials, but her present constraints include rent, school costs, car expenses, and variable work hours (Q56-Q64, Q83). She responds to financial shocks by picking up shifts, cutting discretionary spending, using small savings, and occasionally relying on family help, suggesting practical risk management with limited liquidity (Q60-Q64, Q81-Q82). Peer and community accountability matter: she participates in a small church-based savings circle and is motivated by family, church, and nursing mentors (Q04, Q61). Her relaxed scheduling sometimes creates costs, as shown by a missed school deadline, but she adapts with phone reminders and blocked study time (Q18, Q44).
summaries.political_scientist: Jailyn is a moderate-to-strong Democrat who votes in major elections and is trying to become more consistent in local elections (Q23, Q95-Q96). Her political views center on health care access, racial justice, education, workers' treatment, housing costs, and investment in Black Jacksonville neighborhoods (Q24-Q28). She is civically engaged but not highly partisan online, preferring family conversations, selective social media sharing, volunteering, and occasional protest participation (Q29-Q30, Q48-Q49). Her institutional trust is mixed: she trusts health professionals and public health sources but is attentive to medical mistrust and policing inequities (Q20-Q22, Q41-Q42).
summaries.psychologist: Jailyn presents as calm, resilient, socially embedded, and purpose-driven, with a self-concept built around care work, dignity, faith, and community usefulness (Q01, Q43, Q65, Q109). She has no diagnosed depression or anxiety but reports stress, anxious moments, procrastination, and fatigue when school, work, and money collide (Q43-Q45, Q50). Her coping strategies are relational and embodied: prayer, choir, dance, volleyball, cooking, music, quiet drives, and talking with her mother or roommate (Q38, Q43-Q47, Q50). She is motivated by identity, family responsibility, Black community health equity, and a concrete path toward becoming an RN (Q24, Q35, Q108).
